span.label: mechanisms
span.term: once procedures have been memorised and practised without understanding, students lose the motivation to look for their meaning, which is why a procedure-first sequence blocks the conceptual half of the iteration

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: The paper's claim that misunderstanding of the two knowledge forms is widespread among teachers rests on anecdote rather than on collected data.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper concedes that the concept-first iterative approach it endorses has little empirical evidence behind it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The dichotomy the paper's title turns on is reported as having been declared fundamentally unsound, on the ground that procedures are conceptual in nature.
span.note: what this limits: the conceptual/procedural split as a sound partition: the paper reports Kieran declaring the dichotomy fundamentally unsound because procedures are conceptual during elaboration
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Treating the two knowledge forms as two ends of a continuum is called false; the paper holds that either can occupy different positions depending on the situation.
span.note: what this limits: a placement of a task or a learner at one end of the conceptual/procedural continuum: the paper calls that positioning false, since either can occupy different places depending on the situation
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two cells of Star's own matrix have no worked exemplars - the paper reports that deep-procedural and shallow-conceptual knowledge are hard even to illustrate.

span.label: conceptual knowledge → procedural knowledge
span.note: THE DISTINCTION ITSELF IS DECLARED UNSOUND, and no type can say that. Kieran (2013) 'declared the dichotomy between them to be fundamentally unsound'. `distinct-from` asserts the two ARE distinct; there is no way to record a cited author denying that the boundary can be drawn - the same gap quine1951 sits in.

span.label: concept - a mental representation embodying the essential features of an object, situation or idea, whose function is to let phenomena be classified as belonging together or not
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: procedural knowledge - characterised by some researchers as the capacity to follow steps in sequence to reach a mathematical goal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the conceptual/procedural relation - bi-directional but NOT always symmetrical, with conceptual knowledge at times the stronger support
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conceptual/procedural - a single distinction carrying eight different name pairs across eight traditions (Skemp's instrumental/relational, Tulving's episodic/semantic, Anderson's procedural/declarative...), which the paper asserts are the same division
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: deep - in Star's matrix a property that BOTH knowledge types can have, not a property of conceptual knowledge alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: adaptive expertise - both knowledge types deep AND applicable to unfamiliar situations; routine expertise is the same knowledge without the transfer
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → the belief, held by the experienced teachers the author surveyed, that conceptual and procedural knowledge are mutually exclusive and that conceptual is always the more necessary
span.note: The paper's target is a belief held by practitioners rather than a published claim, and it is quoted from the author's own observation of them.

span.label: conceptual knowledge —renamed-across-fields→ Declarative
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — TABLE 1 IS THIS PROJECT'S THESIS WITH A TABLE. Eight research traditions across 1976-1984 - Skemp, Piaget, Gelman & Gallistel, Resnick, Tulving, Anderson, Van Lehn, Baroody - each name the SAME two categories differently, and the paper says so outright: 'regardless of the labels, the divisions regarding the types of knowledge are consistent'. The claim of sameness is the paper's, not the tagger's.

span.label: Experienced primary and lower-secondary teachers believed that conceptual and procedural knowledge are mutually exclusive and that conceptual knowledge is always the more appropriate thing to teach.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both procedural and conceptual knowledge matter and each reinforces the other, so teaching should aim at both rather than choosing between them.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Either knowledge type can be shallow or deep, so treating conceptual as inherently deep and procedural as inherently shallow misrepresents both.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The synthesis endorses teaching conceptual knowledge before procedural knowledge in most cases.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Starting with conceptual knowledge and moving to procedural knowledge makes conceptual understanding more likely, whereas the procedural-to-conceptual direction risks students never reaching conceptual knowledge.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The empirical support for concept-first is that students taught conceptually and then procedurally outperform students taught procedurally and then conceptually.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Procedural practice only feeds conceptual growth when the problems are sequenced to expose conceptual relationships; randomly ordered problems produced no such effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The conceptual-procedural relationship is bi-directional but asymmetric: conceptual knowledge supports procedural knowledge more strongly and more consistently than procedural supports conceptual.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's answer to its own title is that teachers need conceptual AND procedural knowledge, with the timing and placement left to the teacher's professional judgement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because both knowledge types can occupy different points on a quality continuum, the dichotomy between conceptual and procedural knowledge is judged fundamentally unsound.
